VILLAGE OF BRINKHAVEN | YOUR MUNICIPAL CODE — PLAIN LANGUAGE GUIDE Village of Brinkhaven • Municipal Code Plain Language Guide • Page 6 of 9 Chapter 903 — Blighted Properties A property is “blighted” when its condition constitutes a public nuisance or poses a risk to public health and safety. Blight indicators include structural instability, unsecured or broken openings, accumulation of refuse or junk, overgrown vegetation harboring vermin, infestation, or standing water. When a property is declared blighted, the owner receives written notice with at least 14 days to correct the conditions. If they don’t, the Village can: ▪ Issue citations and fines ▪ Enter the property and perform the abatement itself ▪ Bill the owner for the cost of abatement and, if unpaid, place a lien on the property A vacant structure is any structure unoccupied for more than 90 consecutive days. 6. Code Enforcement Brinkhaven's Code is enforced by a Code Enforcement Officer—a civilian role established under Chapter 307. The officer is responsible for identifying and documenting violations and working with property owners toward resolution. Title XV (General Penalties and Enforcement) governs how violations are handled across the entire Code, including administrative orders, citations, civil remedies, and appeals. Enforcement generally follows a flexible sequence: • A written administrative order identifying the violation and setting a reasonable time to correct it. • An administrative citation if the violation continues or if immediate enforcement is warranted. • Civil or criminal enforcement for violations classified as misdemeanors or where warranted by law. 4. How to Read a Section Every section of the Code follows a consistent format. Here is what the pieces mean: Element What It Means Section Number (e.g., § 901.05) The first digits identify the Title and Chapter; the digits after the decimal identify the specific section. So § 901.05 is Title IX, Chapter 901, Section 5. Section Title A plain-language label for what that section covers. Definitions Many chapters open with a definitions section. Those definitions apply throughout that chapter. Body Text "Shall" means required. "May" means permitted but not required. "Shall not" or "must not" means prohibited. Penalty / Enforcement Some sections specify consequences for violations. General enforcement procedures for the entire Code are found in Title XV. I'm a landlord or absentee owner—do I need to register? Yes. All landlords and absentee property owners (those residing more than 30 miles from Brinkhaven for more than 180 days per year) must register annually with the Village. Registration includes contact information, property details, and an emergency contact. Failure to register is a separate, independently enforceable violation (Chapter 905).
